sequence_description: Direct-endpoint attack: attempt to inject authorization parameters via an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) against a public client. If accepted, Keycloak is consuming a different semantic proof than it verified (no signature verification).
description: [LLM-Judge] The test claims an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) was accepted (HTTP 200), but the client creation failed, so this result is likely not exercising the intended public-client request-object verification path (possible false positive).

sequence_description: I1 direct-endpoint: Cross-client request object confusion. Create two clients; probe whether an unsigned request object (alg=none) is accepted for either client, indicating missing signature verification and potential parameter injection across clients.
description: [LLM-Judge] The request-object tests returned HTTP 200/accepted even though both client creations failed, so the result cannot be attributed to per-client request object signature verification and may indicate the test hit a generic endpoint/page rather than enforcing request-object validation.

evidence.llm_judge_description: The request-object tests returned HTTP 200/accepted even though both client creations failed, so the result cannot be attributed to per-client request object signature verification and may indicate the test hit a generic endpoint/page rather than enforcing request-object validation.

sequence_description: I5: Unsigned request object (alg=none) should not be accepted to inject elevated scopes/claims at the authorization endpoint. Tests whether Keycloak accepts alg=none request objects that could expand effective permissions beyond broker policy.
description: [LLM-Judge] Authorization endpoint appears to accept an unsigned request object (alg=none), but the client creation failed so this may be a false positive due to missing/invalid client configuration.
